chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) visited Khadijah when her son Qasim passed away, and she was crying. So he said to her: 'What makes you cry?' She said: 'The milk flows, so I weep.' He said: 'O Khadijah! Would you not be pleased when it is the Day of Resurrection that you come to the Gate of Paradise and he is standing there, so he takes your hand and enters you into Paradise and settles you in its best part? And that is for every believer. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more Wise and Generous than to deprive the believer of the fruit of his heart and then punish him after it forever.'

key_terms.ثَمَرَةَ فُؤَادِهِ: The fruit of his heart (referring to the beloved deceased)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'fruit of the heart' in Shia theology regarding the death of children?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) comforts Khadijah (AS) by assuring her that Allah, in His generosity, will not punish believers for the natural sorrow of losing a beloved child, but rather reward them in Paradise. This hadith is foundational in Shia theology for understanding *al-huzn* (grief) as a natural, non-punitive emotion, distinguishing it from the loss of faith. It underscores the divine attribute of *Al-Karim* (The Generous), emphasizing that the 'fruit of the heart' is preserved for the believer in the afterlife.
